title: Adding onetouch verio flex?

Okay, thanks, I am working on this now. It appears that the meter doesn't comply with the well established bluetooth standard for glucose meters (that we already support), which means it instead needs special code to handle its *unique* protocol.

I have added support for the Verio Flex with about 500 lines of code in the June 8th nightly. Testing on Android 6 gave good results but I had less luck on Android 4.4. 

I had to alter some of the logic to accommodate it and so pairing and syncing for other devices will also need retesting.  

You need to have at least two blood tests on the meter I think before using the scan option. If it succeeds then you should get a message saying "enabled auto-start"

I found sometimes I had to turn the meter off for a while then turn it back on. Having the meter paired to multiple phones also seemed to cause indigestion.

Please test and let me know how it goes!!

[Mine defaults to insulin frequently, and I'm not on insulin so I'd never input it; this would be an awesome addition also!]

Okay so do you have it now working where you can take a blood test and it will automatically connect to the phone (while the phone is screen off) and sync that latest reading?

Another caveat is that there are some issues with the time synchronization. It will cause problems if the clock on the meter is changed when data hasn't been synced or on a new pairing to a phone where any of the last 15 readings had a different meter clock at the time of the test. 

It works by reading the current meter time and then calculating how different that is to the current phone time to calculate when the blood test actually occurred.  So long as you are always synced before changing the meter clock this shouldn't create any issues.  I am assuming the meter doesn't automatically adjust for daylight saving time.

If you're talking about the xDrip facebook group, I haven't ever been on there. I rely on other people to communicate there.

I have not tried with the phone screen off yet. I will tonight.

What else can I test for you?

You should get to a stage where use of the meter with xDrip is completely seamless. Whenever you do a test you will get it syncing to the phone and with the automatic calibration enabled it will cherry pick the best values to use for calibration. If you are away from the phone then when you next turn on the meter or do a blood test it should sync all the previous readings (up to a maximum of approx 15 readings)

It should work when the screen is off and you shouldn't need to open xDrip app for the data to be synced and it should just work in the background forever. Those sorts of things over an extended period is what needs testing. Some of this depends on the quality of the phone bluetooth stack. The sound effects feature helps you know when its doing something even when the screen is off. You can turn this off if it bugs you.

Also you can check in the event log as you shouldn't get any entries relating to the glucose meter show up as these would normally indicate an unexpected error.

I have been using my Contour Next One meter.  I just updated to this latest version, and that meter is still working.  I also have a Verio Flex meter.  I intend to test that meter as well.  However, What problems can I expect to encounter when switching from the Contour to the Verio?  Earlier you mentioned there were problems relating to the clock on the meter - should I adjust the Verio meter clock before attempting the first sync?

@TecMunky no sync before changing the clock. xDrip will work out the correct time from the offset of the meter clock from its clock but it can't do this if the clock was changed before the sync occurs, so always sync before changing the meter time. xDrip wont try to sync readings it already has so any clock confusion wont matter after a sync has occurred. The meter itself doesn't get confused but I don't really see how this is represented in the data and as the protocol is unique and undocumented I did the best I could as it seemed like a fairly small issue which shouldn't affect people during day to day use.

Well it's working good for now; even did a double calibration with it automatically.

The issues you've experienced may be due to android bluetooth flaking out.

Next time you don't get it syncing, try this, go in to the settings for the bluetooth glucose meter in xdrip and slide the slider at the top for off/on to turn it off and on again. Then see if it syncs after that. If it does then it implies we're losing the bluetooth connection after a while.

The meter doesn't push the data to the app, the app detects the bluetooth being enabled and the remote device coming on and then connects to it to ask for the data. The sync icon you see appears on the meter when it detects the app connecting and asking for data.
